questions.q: Who was the Mongol ruler that invaded Delhi in 1398, causing great destruction?
questions.a: The ruler was Timur (also known as Tamerlane). A wrong answer suggests the student is confusing the timeline with earlier Mongol raids or later invaders like the Mughals.

questions.q: Why did the death of Firuz Shah Tughlaq act as a turning point for the Sultanate?
questions.a: It led to succession disputes, meaning different people fought to be the next Sultan instead of working together. A wrong answer suggests a lack of understanding that stable leadership is required to keep a large empire united.

questions.q: If you were a provincial governor at the time of Timur’s invasion, how would the weakened state of the Delhi government affect your loyalty to the Sultan?
questions.a: Steps: 1. Recognize the Sultan can no longer protect your region. 2. Realize the central government is disorganized. 3. Conclude that you might stop sending taxes or following orders. 4. Decide to rule independently. A wrong answer shows the student assumes blind loyalty even when the central authority has failed.

questions.q: How did the transition from the Tughlaq dynasty to the Sayyid dynasty reflect the changing power of the Sultanate?
questions.a: The Sayyid dynasty controlled a much smaller territory than the Tughlaqs, showing the Sultanate was shrinking. A wrong answer indicates the student thinks the Sultanate remained strong and stable throughout all dynasties.

questions.q: Was Timur’s invasion the only reason the Sultanate declined? Explain.
questions.a: No, the Sultanate was already weak due to internal fighting and succession disputes before Timur arrived. Timur’s invasion was the final blow that made recovery impossible. A wrong answer shows the student fails to see the difference between a long-term problem and a final collapse.

questions.q: Imagine you are writing a history report; what evidence would you use to show that the Delhi Sultanate was no longer the powerful force it once was by the time of the Lodi dynasty?
questions.a: The student should mention the reduced size of the territory and the frequent changes in dynasties. A poor answer focuses on irrelevant facts like the architecture or personal lives of the rulers rather than the loss of power.
